title: SCIM ordered-retry + audit trail for eventual consistency of user & group state
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Background: Customers have reported edge cases where SCIM changes (user create, attribute updates, group membership changes, and deprovisioning) appear out-of-order or temporarily missing in Redwood due to upstream identity provider retries, transient networking, or rate-limited responses. This causes RBAC misalignment, stale audit state, and incorrect billing traces. Goal: Implement an ordered-retry + audit-correlation mechanism for SCIM events that ensures eventual consistency for user and group state across hosts and surfaces an auditable, queryable trail in the Console. Approach balances reliability (at-least-once delivery + idempotency) with latency and storage cost by using ordered sequence numbers, tombstones for deprovisioned identities, adaptive retry/backoff, and an audit correlation ID propagated through the provisioning pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: SCIM POST/PUT/DELETE requests carry a client-provided idempotency key and server-assigned sequence number preserved through retries
User and group state in the primary datastore converges to the identity provider state within the configured reconciliation window (default 10 minutes) after injected transient failures
Deprovisioning operations produce tombstone records (retained 30 days) and write an audit event with correlation_id visible in Console logs
Retries are ordered for a given identity: later sequence numbers never get applied before earlier ones; out-of-order deliveries are buffered or rejected with metrics
Operational dashboard shows SCIM retry rate, backlog queue depth, tombstone counts, reconciliation job lag, and a new SLO: 99% convergence within 10 minutes
A small-scale canary rollout (5% orgs) shows no increase in user-facing auth failures and reduces manual reconciliation incidents in pilot customers
Documentation and runbook added; security review completed and signed off
design_notes: Attach an ordered_sequence (monotonic integer per identity) to every incoming SCIM change; if IdP doesn't provide sequence, generate using last-seen+1 with optimistic locking

Implement per-identity write-ahead buffer: writes with sequence <= applied_sequence are no-ops (idempotent); writes with sequence == applied_sequence + 1 are applied; writes with sequence > applied_sequence + 1 are buffered for up to 10 minutes and trigger reconciliation
Introduce a tombstone flag and tombstone_expiry timestamp on user/group records to handle deprovisioning while retaining audit trail and preventing resurrection during late retries
Propagate a correlation_id through gateway -> provisioning service -> datastore -> event-emitter; correlation_id surfaces in Console trace and audit logs for end-to-end investigation

Adaptive retry/backoff: exponential backoff with jitter, but limit attempts per identity per minute and surface to SLA team; on repeated failure escalate to dead-letter queue (DLQ) with metadata (last_seq, attempts, reason)
Prefer strong consistency for sequence checks using lightweight conditional writes (optimistic concurrency) to avoid global locks; fall back to reconciliation job for missed windows
Store buffered/out-of-order events in a partitioned queue (by identity hash) with TTL and replay path; this keeps hot identity operations isolated
Trade-offs: buffering increases memory/disk usage and complexity but avoids noisy full-table reconciliation. Tombstones add storage but are necessary for security/audit compliance
implementation_plan: API: extend SCIM endpoint to accept optional client_sequence and client_correlation_id; validate headers and return assigned server_sequence
Runtime: add sequence-aware write middleware to provisioning service (provisioner v2). Implement optimistic compare-and-swap to apply changes atomically
Buffer: implement per-identity buffer in Redis streams with size limits; ensure partitioning by identity id to preserve order
Tombstones: add tombstone boolean and expiry timestamp to user/group schema; migration script to backfill existing deprovisioned users
DLQ: create dead-letter table and retry controller; surface DLQ items to Console with one-click requeue for SRE
Audit: emit structured audit events (JSON) including correlation_id, server_sequence, client_sequence, actor, and change_summary to existing audit pipeline
Console: add a SCIM provisioning dashboard: retry rate, buffer depth, DLQ count, reconciliation lag, tombstone retention
Docs & Runbook: draft runbook for SRE and Support with query examples to find correlation_id traces
Security: complete threat model and get security review; use KMS for any sensitive payloads in logs
testing_plan: Unit tests for sequence logic, tombstone semantics, and idempotency no-op behavior
Integration tests that simulate out-of-order deliveries, network partitions, and IdP retry storms
Load test that exercises hot identities to validate buffer partitioning and latency under 95th/99th percentiles
Chaos test: kill provisioning instances mid-apply to ensure replay and reconciliation converge
End-to-end canary with two pilot customers' IdPs to validate Console traceability and no auth regressions
Security test: verify no sensitive fields exposed in audit events and that tombstone expiry respects retention policy
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the sequence enforcement behind config scim.v2.sequence_enforcement = off by default
Step 1: deploy to staging and run full test-suite; validate metrics and DLQ behavior
Step 2: enable for internal Redwood orgs and observe for 72 hours
Step 3: enable 5% of customers (canary); monitor convergence SLO and auth error rates; threshold: <0.1% increase in auth failures
Step 4: if canary healthy, ramp to 25% and run overnight reconciliation; if stable, schedule full rollout
Rollback: flip scim.v2.sequence_enforcement=false and requeue DLQ items; run global reconciliation as safety net
Post-rollout: run a 30-day tombstone retention audit and remove expired tombstones per policy
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: scim.server_sequence_gap_count – count of buffered events where server_sequence < event.sequence
Metric: scim.retries_per_identity.p95 – signal retry storms; alert if >50 for any identity in 1h
Metric: scim.dlq_count – critical alert if sustained > 100 items for >30m
Metric: scim.reconciliation_lag_seconds – warn at >600s, critical at >1800s
Log: audit events indexed by correlation_id; Console query template for 'correlation_id:<id>'
SLO: 99% of identity changes converge within 10 minutes; alert when window breached for >5% of changes in 1h
